1. (Currently amended) A battery assembly comprising: an enclosure; a first battery cell positioned within the enclosure; and a first sensor positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, wherein the first sensor is configured to detect at least one force influencing the first battery cell.

2. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising an adhesive layer positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the adhesive layer and the enclosure, and wherein the adhesive layer is configured to allow the first sensor to detect deformation of the first battery cell.

3. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein at least a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned adjacent at least a portion of the first sensor in a plane between the first battery cell and the enclosure, and wherein the adhesive layer maintains contact with the first battery cell while permitting force transmission to the first sensor.

4. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 3, wherein the adhesive layer extends around at least a portion of the first sensor in the plane while maintaining a sensing interface between the first sensor and the first battery cell.

5. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein a portion of the first sensor extends through a gap in the adhesive layer towards an edge of the first battery cell to directly contact the first battery cell.

6. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned between the first sensor and one of the first battery cell and the enclosure, and wherein another portion of the first sensor is in direct contact with the first battery cell.

7. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising a deformable element positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the deformable element, and wherein the deformable element is configured to transmit forces from the first battery cell to the first sensor.

8. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein: the enclosure comprises an enclosure portion of protective film; the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure portion; and the protective film is configured to allow force transmission from the first battery cell to the first sensor.

9. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 8, wherein the protective film is a polyester film having a thickness configured to permit force sensing.

10. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein: the enclosure comprises a plastic case portion; the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the plastic case portion; and the plastic case portion is configured to allow force transmission from the first battery cell to the first sensor.

11. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising a second battery cell stacked on top of the first battery cell, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the second battery cell, and wherein the first sensor is configured to detect forces between the stacked battery cells.

12. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 11 further comprising an adhesive layer between the first battery cell and the second battery cell, wherein the adhesive layer is configured to allow the first sensor to detect compression forces between the stacked cells.

13. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein at least a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned adjacent at least a portion of the first sensor in a plane between the first battery cell and the second battery cell, and wherein the adhesive layer maintains force transmission to the first sensor.

14. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 13, wherein the adhesive layer extends around at least a portion of the first sensor in the plane while maintaining a sensing interface.

15. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein a portion of the first sensor extends through a gap in the adhesive layer towards an edge of the first battery cell to directly contact the first battery cell.

16. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned between the first sensor and one of the first battery cell and the second battery cell, and wherein another portion of the first sensor is in direct contact with the first battery cell.

17. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising: a second battery cell stacked on top of the first battery cell, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the second battery cell; a third battery cell stacked on top of the second battery cell; and a second sensor positioned between the third battery cell and the second battery cell for detecting at least one force influencing the third battery cell, wherein the first and second sensors are independently configured to detect forces in their respective positions.

18. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 17 further comprising a processor configured to: receive a first sensor output signal from the first sensor indicating forces on the first battery cell; receive a second sensor output signal from the second sensor indicating forces on the third battery cell; conduct an evaluation based at least on the received output signals and the relative magnitudes of forces detected; and generate at least one processor output signal based on the evaluation.

19. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 18, wherein the processor is further configured to alter an operation of the third battery cell independently from an operation of the first battery cell based on the at least one processor output signal when the second sensor detects forces exceeding a threshold.

20. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 18, wherein the processor is further configured to turn off the third battery cell and to maintain operation of the first battery cell based on the at least one processor output signal when the second sensor detects forces indicating swelling or deformation of the third battery cell.

21. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein the first sensor comprises: force sensing material having a conductance that is configured to vary based on the at least one force influencing the first battery cell; and force sensing circuitry coupled to the force sensing material, wherein the force sensing circuitry is configured to produce a force output signal based on the conductance of the force sensing material, and wherein the force sensing material is positioned to directly contact the first battery cell.

22. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 21, wherein the force sensing material comprises at least one variable electrical conductor in direct contact with the first battery cell.

23. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 22, wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor has a first level of electrical conductance when the at least one variable electrical conductor is quiescent, and wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor has a second level of conductance when a mechanical stress from the first battery cell is applied to the at least one variable electrical conductor.

24. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 22, wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor is a quantum tunneling composite material positioned to detect swelling or deformation of the first battery cell.

25. (Cancelled)

26. (Cancelled)

27. (Cancelled)

28. (Original) A method for monitoring a battery comprising a first cell and a second cell stacked within an enclosure, the method comprising: positioning a first sensor material between the first cell and one of the second cell and the enclosure; varying the conductance of the first material based on at least one force influencing the first cell; and producing a first force output signal based on the conductance of the first material.

29. (Original) The method of claim 28 further comprising controlling a facility of the first cell based on the force output signal.

30. (Original) The method of claim 28 further comprising: receiving a battery status signal, wherein the battery status signal is responsive to at least one of a voltage, a current, and a temperature of the first cell; evaluating the first force output signal and the battery status signal; and generating at least one evaluated output signal based on the evaluation of the first force output signal and the battery status signal.
